description: A dermatologist-inspired routine designed to soothe and hydrate the skin, reducing the severity of eczema symptoms.
frequency: Daily (morning and night) with weekly treatments.

morning_steps.action: Cleanse the face with a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser.
morning_steps.purpose: Remove any oils and impurities from the skin without causing irritation.

morning_steps.action: Apply a hydrating toner to restore the skin's pH balance.
morning_steps.purpose: Help maintain the skin barrier and reduce redness.

morning_steps.action: Moisturize with an oil-free, fragrance-free moisturizer that is suitable for sensitive skin.
morning_steps.purpose: Lock in moisture to keep the skin hydrated and reduce dryness.

night_steps.action: Cleansing the face with a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser.
night_steps.purpose: Remove any oils and impurities from the skin without causing irritation.

night_steps.action: Apply a hydrating toner to restore the skin's pH balance.
night_steps.purpose: Help maintain the skin barrier and reduce redness.

night_steps.action: Moisturize with a richer, fragrance-free moisturizer to lock in moisture overnight.
night_steps.purpose: Provide deep hydration as the skin repairs itself during sleep.

night_steps.action: Consider applying a corticosteroid cream or ointment if prescribed by your dermatologist, being careful not to overuse it.
night_steps.purpose: Reduce inflammation and itching as directed by your healthcare provider.

weekly_steps.action: Apply a thick barrier cream or ointment like an emollient to the skin, especially on areas affected by eczema.

do: Use lukewarm water for facial cleansers and baths.
Wear loose-fitting clothing made of soft fabrics like cotton.
Avoid harsh soaps and detergents that can strip natural oils from the skin.
dont: Rub or scratch affected areas, as this can worsen eczema.
Use products with fragrance, alcohol, or other irritants.
Exfoliate the skin vigorously, which can be too harsh for sensitive skin.
common_mistakes: Over-washing or scrubbing the skin can disrupt its protective barrier and exacerbate symptoms.
Neglecting to moisturize regularly, leading to dryness and irritation.
Using products with irritating ingredients without consulting a dermatologist.

expected_results.2_weeks: Reduction in dryness and itching, less visible redness.
expected_results.1_month: Significant improvement in skin hydration and reduced flakiness, fewer outbreaks.
expected_results.3_months: Sustained relief from eczema symptoms with minimal flare-ups.

expert_tips: Always patch test new skincare products before incorporating them into your routine to ensure they are well-tolerated by your skin.
Keep a journal of your diet, environment, and product use to identify potential triggers and adjust your routine accordingly.
Stay consistent with your skincare regimen for the best long-term results.
